name: Joeser
title: Jacob's son and Egypt's wise man
summary: Joseph (Joeser) was the eleventh son of the patriarch Jacob and his wife Rachel. He was sold into slavery by his jealous brothers, but rose to become the second most powerful man in Egypt after interpreting Pharaoh's dreams. Through his position, he saved his family and all of Egypt from famine, and he is a model of forgiveness and God's providence.

keyEvents.title: Joseph's Dreams
keyEvents.description: As a young boy, Joseph dreamed that his brothers' sheaves and the stars of heaven bowed down to him, which aroused his brothers' jealousy.

keyEvents.title: Sold as a Slave
keyEvents.description: Joseph's brothers sold him to Midianite merchants who took him to Egypt, where he was sold to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials.

keyEvents.title: In Prison and Interpreting Dreams
keyEvents.description: After being falsely accused by Potiphar's wife, Joseph was thrown into prison, where he interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh's Dreams and Exaltation
keyEvents.description: Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams about seven years of plenty and seven years of famine, and was appointed to rule over all Egypt as the second most powerful person after Pharaoh.

keyEvents.title: Reunion with His Brothers
keyEvents.description: During the famine, Joseph's brothers came to Egypt to buy grain. After testing them, Joseph revealed his identity and forgave them with tears.

keyEvents.title: Joseph as an Example of Faith
keyEvents.description: In Hebrews, Joseph is mentioned as an example of faith, for on his deathbed he spoke about the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones.
